chapter: CBS, return to Ellington and retirement
title: The trombone section on his return
summary: He names Booty Wood and Britt Woodman, Britt's trombonist father, and Butter Jackson.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Who was in the trombone section when
Oh, Buster Cooper -- oh --

According to a chart I have here prepared by a Frenchman by the name of Jean Portier which is reasonably accurate, it says when you returned to the band in 1960 the other two trombone players were Mitchell Booty Wood D'Letwood and Britt Woodman?

Yes, that's possibly the right ones although there were quite a few changes after that. Booty, his wife, got ill, and he had to return home. And Britt he changed and he quit and he went into something else, and those kinds of things, you know.
Had you known Britt in Los Angeles when you lived here?
I knew his father.
His father was a musician?
Was a musician. He was a trombone player too. He worked down at the -- what is that vaudeville theater down on Main Street -- yeah, he was a very good musician.
What was his first name?
His father's first name?
(inaudible). I've heard it, but I can't remember
Yeah, I can't remember it right now.
And then he had one brother at least -- was it more than one brother who was also a musician?
They had -- his brother Woodman and Brit Woodman -- they had a group or something.
Yes, uh-huh.
(inaudible). in Los Angeles when they were youngsters?
Right. I forget the -- I'm getting too old.
So, you worked with Beaty Bowie and Britt, and let's see, Butter had left the year before, right? Yeah.
Yes.
You had worked with Butter --
I worked with Butter a little while.
I think But not in 1960, because Apparently if you left he in '59, and that was to go join Quincy Jones --
Quincy Jones. They went to Europe. That's right.
But you worked with Butter up until the time you left before, because you were with Butter in the '40s and --
Right. Right. Uh-huh.
